newsitem.title: UK: Airlines & forwarders must cooperate-Cargolux boss.
newsitem.headline: Airlines & forwarders must cooperate-Cargolux boss.

text.p: Airlines and forwarders must cooperate more on services and information if they are to fend off the integrators, warned Robert Arendal, senior vice-president of cargo for Cargolux Airlines S.A.

Speaking at an air cargo conference in London, Arendal said that airlines and forwarders need to cooperate more fully, otherwise Fedex, TNT, DHL and UPS, may increase their share of the heavy air cargo market.
Airfreight forwarders, not shippers, are likely to continue to arrange the transportation of most large airfreight shipments.
But new technology makes it possible for shippers to participate more actively than ever before in the transportation process, he added.
"They can become minutely involved in the selection of the mode of transportation, schedule, routing of their shipments and even chosing the individual carriers."
Shippers want more control and more information and new technologies can provide both.
"For airlines and forwarders that work in partnership, this is an opportunity to offer one-stop services," Arendal told delegates.
Manufacturers want to cut costs by reducing inventories and by using just-in-time techniques and thus need a finely tuned logistics system that relies on intensive information flows.
Forwarders and carriers must be able to feed data into shippers systems, he stressed.
Many air cargo vendors have not yet grasped the significance of these new technologies or the need to cooperate in bringing a unified interface to the shipper, he noted.
Bar code use must be increased as a means to identify airfreight shipments and the Cargolux boss said he was frustrated at the industry's inability to make better use of bar codes.
"As an industry we lack the leadership needed for widespread and effective use of bar codes," he stressed to delegates.
Both airlines and forwarders have wasted millions of dollars developing EDI systems and yet the Internet is now opening comunications links to everyone.

Shippers will insist on more transparent systems that give them greater control and information in order to reduce their own manufacturing costs. Lower costs are vital in order to be competitive, he added.
The industry should improve the quality of air cargo transporation and reduce total transit times.

Shippers pay the cost of transportation but the cost of implementing information systems is high so Arendal said it could be that shippers, forwarders and airlines will have to share the burden of its development and operation.
